title: Remaining-power edits overwrite capacity
evidence: For GenFuellessGenerator, GenCompGenerator and GenSpaceDrive, start at capacity 1000 / remaining 250 and set POWERREM=40. Each ends at capacity 40 / remaining 250. Their POWERREM setter branches call setPowerCapacity.
impact: Builder edits and generic field restoration can corrupt both a component budget and its saved configuration. Remaining power may exceed capacity.
repair: Correct the three setters; audit sibling generic fields and specify bounds without silently destroying recoverable legacy data.
acceptance: Each independent field edit and XML round trip preserves the other fields, including a non-full device. Migration reports invalid legacy values.

title: Fractional recharge settings are rounded to integers
evidence: GenComputerConsole.setStat(RECHRATE, 0.5) produces 1. Its parser is s_parseLongExpression, which rounds; several generator and thruster setters use the same integer parser. This is rounding, not always truncation to zero.
impact: A half-rate console becomes full-rate. Small nonzero authored rates can become zero. Not every component is affected: GenSpaceDrive uses the floating parser for this field.
repair: Use the floating expression parser consistently and validate finite nonnegative rates with a documented upper-bound policy.
acceptance: 0.1, 0.5 and 1.25 survive edits and export/import within float tolerance for all affected generic classes.

title: Gravity generators identify and compare as other component types
evidence: StdShipGravityGen reports SHIP_ENVIRO_CONTROL; two fresh gravity generators return sameAs=false. getTechType returns the environment category and sameAs tests StdShipDampener.
impact: Typed installation panels and manufacturer matching can reject or misclassify gravity generators. Equality checks misreport differences.
repair: Use SHIP_GRAVGEN, fix the equality guard, and diagnose existing panels that were authored around the wrong category.
acceptance: The generator fits its declared gravity panel, compares equal to an identical generator, and restores under a documented legacy category policy.

title: Health scans report zero percent for wounded targets
evidence: A target at 50/100 HP reports health: 0%. HealthScanProgram divides two integer HP values before converting the result to a percentage.
impact: Medical tools give misleading information at almost every non-full health value. A zero maximum is also unguarded in this expression.
repair: Perform guarded floating division and keep percentages consistent with textual health descriptions.
acceptance: 0/100, 1/100, 50/100, 100/100 and an invalid zero maximum produce meaningful bounded output without an arithmetic exception.

title: Coordinate service handlers are not advertised
evidence: DatabaseProgram advertises only IDENTIFICATION; ShipSensorProgram advertises no services. Both contain COORDQUERY handlers. GenShipProgram.findCoordinates uses the service registry. Scoped Java search found no advertised COORDQUERY provider.
impact: The named coordinate lookup path used by navigation cannot reach these handlers. This does not establish that every COURSE command is broken: direct contact targeting follows other paths.
repair: Advertise the intended service, validate request/response formats, and test both database and sensed-contact lookups.
acceptance: A known beacon resolves through a real installed service, an unknown beacon fails clearly, and the result is isolated to the correct computer/circuit.

title: Database custom fields read NOTE instead of their own value
evidence: Rendering a database entry with NAME and CUSTOM but no NOTE throws NullPointerException. getSpaceObjectDataResults reads jo.get(NOTE).toString() in the loop for every non-basic field.
impact: Authored logs and star-chart metadata can break the terminal display. Adding NOTE masks the exception but repeats the note instead of each custom value.
repair: Render the actual key value, define null/missing-field display, and preserve unknown fields across exports.
acceptance: Two distinct custom fields, absent NOTE, null values and Unicode text render correctly without losing data.

title: Engine profiling shares charts and turning capability is over-reported
evidence: ShipNavProgram creates accelValues once outside its engine loop and EngProfile retains that array. fasterTurns ends with true even if no inertial component qualifies; its conditional also has mixed &&/|| precedence.
impact: Autopilot can plan using the last profiled engine for every engine and assume fast turns without working inertial support. No complete flight was run for this finding.
repair: Allocate each chart independently, make profiling non-destructive, and make capability decisions explicit.
acceptance: A mixed two-engine vessel keeps distinct profiles; removing or disabling its inertial device changes the turn plan. Profiling restores thrust, fuel and flight state.

title: The no-landing-zone path constructs a track with null
evidence: landProcedure can construct ShipNavTrack(LAND, programPlanet, engines, null). ShipNavTrack immediately calls getClass on each supplied argument, including the null LocationRoom.
impact: Landing near an otherwise eligible body with no authored landing room can throw instead of returning a useful rejection. The complete command path was not executed.
repair: Refuse the missing destination before track construction, or model an optional destination explicitly and define the fallback.
acceptance: Landing on a body with zero, one, multiple and removed landing zones either succeeds at a legal zone or leaves the ship safely under control with a clear reason.

title: Sensor aiming repeats the second direction
evidence: ShipSensorProgram sends dirs.get(0), then uses dirs.get(1) on every iteration of a loop whose index advances through all remaining directions.
impact: A three-direction scan omits its third requested direction. Wider scan configurations do not match the command.
repair: Use the loop index and validate permitted directional sets before sending commands.
acceptance: A three-direction aim sends all three distinct directions once and rejects unsupported directions without partial retargeting.

title: Optical contacts use the screen and angular sizes use integer division
evidence: The viewscreen converter reports an Asteroid named audit asteroid as an item. Its nested proxy captures inherited me, the screen, rather than the convert argument. Separately, GenShipOpticalSensor computes atan(radius/distance) with long division on both operands; this second issue is static.
impact: Screens misidentify contacts; small foreground objects can spuriously hide larger targets because both angular sizes round to zero. Zero-distance division also needs a policy.
repair: Capture the actual contact, use floating angular comparisons, and refresh directional caches after builder changes.
acceptance: Two distinct contacts retain their own identities; a smaller apparent occluder does not fully hide a larger one; coincident/overlapping objects do not crash.

title: Limited shield coverage can index before the array
evidence: With StdShipShieldGenerator limited to three directions, repeatedly clearing/rebuilding coverage produced 10 index errors in 32 attempts at seed 42. The coverage loop reads centralIndex-offset without wrapping the index.
impact: A valid partial-coverage shield can throw during an incoming attack. Full coverage avoids this particular branch.
repair: Share a bounds-safe arc implementation between weapons, sensors and shields, with explicit count and cache invalidation rules.
acceptance: Every center/count combination from zero through six has defined output, no duplicate arcs, no exception and the requested count where legal.

title: Panel power accounting has two consumers for one allocation
evidence: StdCompPanel inherits StdElecCompContainer.okMessage, which consumes its powerNeeds from the incoming power message into the panel store. Its executeMsg then distributes the remaining message to contents and powerNeeds is their aggregate demand.
impact: Read literally, a panel can charge itself for child demand before forwarding that demand. Conservation across nested panels is uncertain; no full circuit-flow probe was run.
repair: Confirm with a one-source/one-panel/one-load fixture, then give panels one forwarding/accounting responsibility. Treat storage as an explicit component.
acceptance: For flat and nested networks: initial store plus generation equals final store plus useful consumption plus declared loss; under-supply is allocated once.

title: Efficiency and reliability have contradictory meanings
evidence: Manufacturer documents efficiency as a cost (0.5 better, 2 worse). Some generation/charging/shield paths multiply output by it, while other consumers multiply cost or divide fuel use. Personal shielding tests random >= reliability*0.5 plus tech difference, making higher reliability block less in the base shield.
impact: Manufacturer quality has no coherent balance contract. Blindly reversing every multiplier would change existing content in incompatible ways.
repair: Specify separate quality, efficiency/cost and reliability semantics, keep a legacy calculation mode for migrated content, and inventory all consumers.
acceptance: A documented manufacturer matrix shows monotonic improvements in the new model, bounded probabilities and explicit legacy behavior for old worlds.

title: Combat validation mutates resources and item destruction casts items to mobs
evidence: StdGun.okMessage spends ammunition before later listeners can veto. Personal shields also spend power and emit output in okMessage. StdElecWeapon item-target DISINTEGRATE/DISRUPT branches cast the Item target to MOB to find a room.
impact: A vetoed attack can spend ammunition or shield charge. If the item-target damage branch is reached, the cast throws. End-to-end reachability of that special mode was not established.
repair: Separate validation, resource reservation and committed resolution. Resolve item location through the map API instead of assuming a character target.
acceptance: A late veto spends nothing; an accepted attack spends once; a disintegrated item in a room, container or inventory follows the chosen legal policy without a cast exception.

title: An undercharged energy weapon avoids normal damage scaling
evidence: In StdElecWeapon TYP_DAMAGE, sufficient charge subtracts cost and applies successFactor to damage. Insufficient positive charge empties the store but leaves the incoming damage unchanged.
impact: The last undercharged shot can be stronger than a normally powered shot. The intended weak-shot versus refusal policy is undefined.
repair: Choose an explicit insufficient-charge policy per weapon; apply the normal modifiers in every allowed resolution path.
acceptance: At cost-1, cost and cost+1 stored charge, damage and resource consumption match the authored policy and never reward a power shortfall.

title: Inertial braking removes full speed even without sufficient power
evidence: StdShipInertialBattery initializes removedSpeed to ship.speed. Its only reduction branch requires retainingDelta>0, but the earlier guard ensures delta>=pi/2, so retainingDelta<=0. The failure branch changes stored power without limiting removedSpeed.
impact: A qualifying braking activation can stop the entire ship independently of available charge. No dynamic braking fixture was run.
repair: Calculate affordable absorbed energy/speed under a documented arcade model, or model a bounded assist. Keep arc and direction semantics explicit.
acceptance: Zero, partial and sufficient charge produce correspondingly bounded braking, no negative stores, and consistent feedback to autopilot.

title: Intercept and safe-trajectory helpers do not satisfy their contracts
evidence: A runner at (0,0,0), speed 1 along +X, and a chaser at (10,0,0), maximum speed 2, yields no intercept although contact is possible within ten ticks. Static checks also find canMaybeIntercept using runnerO for both start spheres, missing discriminant/horizon checks, and isSafeTrajectory comparing distance from the starting point rather than clearance from obstacles.
impact: Torpedoes and tactical software depend on incorrect interception. The misleading safety helper should not become the basis for a new autopilot. A source search found no production caller of isSafeTrajectory in this baseline.
repair: Define one analytical relative-motion contract with radius, horizon and stationary cases; implement actual swept obstacle clearance or withdraw the unsafe API.
acceptance: Known reachable/unreachable intercepts, tangencies, equal speeds, stationary bodies, horizon expiry and translation/rotation invariance pass independent mathematical checks.

title: Galaxy sectors overflow and space time units disagree
evidence: getSectorName/getInSectorCoords/getSectorMap compute 2L*GalaxyRadius.dm before division. Twice the declared radius exceeds signed long. SpaceObject documents velocity per second, while moveSpaceObject/runSpace apply it per space tick without elapsed-second conversion.
impact: Sector names/maps can be wrong, and a tick-duration change alters physical speed. Approximate masses and gravity are deliberate simplifications, but the unit contract is inconsistent.
repair: Use safe exact sector arithmetic; version sector semantics for existing coordinates. Pick distance/time units explicitly and introduce elapsed-time conversion with a compatibility mode.
acceptance: Boundary, origin, negative-coordinate and extreme-coordinate sector cases agree; moving for equal simulated seconds under two tick durations gives the same displacement in the new mode.

title: Ship damage has explicit unfinished subsystem and inertia work
evidence: GenSpaceShip still marks inertia/g-force damage during acceleration and non-collision internal-system damage as TODO. StdSpaceShip does implement gravity and some high-thrust crew messaging/damage, so these are incomplete pathways, not a total absence of g-force effects.
impact: Creators cannot reliably author targeted reactor/engine failures, localized breaches or a consistent acceleration injury model using hull damage alone.
repair: Define a damage pipeline with optional compartment/subsystem routing and shared crew acceleration events. Reuse existing combat and hull behavior as the simple mode.
acceptance: A chosen subsystem hit changes that subsystem, damage-control actions recover it, and hull/crew effects are ordered and saved without duplicate kill/loot credit.

title: Ship identity changes do not consistently rebuild circuits and caches
evidence: GenSpaceShip.rename calls unregisterElectronics(null, oldKey), but GroundWired unregisters only a non-null component. GenSpaceShip.getShipSensors caches its first list without an invalidation path in that class. StdElecCompItem registers room-owned components before an installation requirement is enforced.
impact: A rename or refit can leave stale topology/contact lists, and merely dropping a component may register it. Actual post-rename failures depend on later re-registration; that full lifecycle was not played.
repair: Use persistent vessel/component IDs, distinct installed membership, and topology generation numbers. Rebuild caches on rename, move, install/remove, copy and restore.
acceptance: Rename a powered vessel, replace a sensor, move a loose component and restore; registry membership remains unique and software sees the current installed equipment.

title: Saved physical motion is ahead of saved software activity state
evidence: A ShipNavProgram with courseSet=true returns courseSet=false after text()/setMiscText round trip. navTrack/course/courseTarget are ordinary runtime fields; no state serialization for them was found in that class or the inspected save adapters. WorldState separately saves NavigableItem travel, which is not this software state.
impact: The engine preserves physical space objects but has no demonstrated resumable ship-autopilot contract. This narrow probe is not a fresh-process campaign restore test and does not prove every program field is lost.
repair: Define persisted navigation/activity state with stable target/component IDs and relative deadlines; either resume validated tracks or restore to a visible safe hold.
acceptance: Fresh-process saves during launch, approach, orbit and landing preserve or safely suspend intended behavior, with one active job and explicit recovery for missing targets.

title: Save warnings still say all space objects are lost
evidence: An asteroid is returned by WorldFiles.spaceItems while WorldState.notKept simultaneously warns that things in space are not saved where they are. Help repeats the old limitation despite SPACE capture/restore and space.cmare.
impact: SAVES CHECK undermines a feature already implemented, making genuine omissions harder to identify.
repair: Generate diagnostics from the actual save coverage rules and update help. Keep precise warnings for remaining unsupported state.
acceptance: A supported unowned asteroid has no blanket loss warning; an intentionally unsupported object/activity reports its exact missing state.

title: Several technology categories have no concrete implementation
evidence: PERSONAL_TRACTOR, PERSONAL_ATMOSUIT, SHIP_TRACTOR, SHIP_REPLICATOR and COMP_PROBE appear in Technical.TechType. Scoped source searches found enum/panel/filter references but no concrete device returning these categories in the technology item families.
impact: An editor category can suggest a working tractor, suit, replicator or exploration probe when it is only a vocabulary slot. Other existing properties can approximate parts of these concepts.
repair: Mark unsupported categories in creator documentation and validators; implement each only as a selected proposal with its own actual behavior.
acceptance: The capability reference distinguishes category-only entries, and newly selected devices have use, power, failure, save and script contracts.

title: Manufacturers and technology progress are installation-wide assets
evidence: GroundWired reads/writes /resources/tech/manufacturers.xml (falling back to examples) and stores global technology values through Resources property data. No world-owned manufacturer/technology manifest or dedicated campaign-state adapter was found in WorldFiles/WorldState/WorldSettings.
impact: Two worlds sharing one engine installation cannot cleanly ship different manufacturer rules. Runtime research/progress would have no clear world-versus-save ownership boundary.
repair: Add world asset resolution for manufacturer/technology definitions; keep immutable world eras distinct from saved campaign discoveries. Migrate legacy resources with explicit precedence.
acceptance: Two worlds with the same manufacturer ID load different definitions without cross-contamination; restoring one campaign restores its discoveries without changing another world.

title: The inherited telnet program connects to real hosts
evidence: ShipTelnetProgram implements ArchonOnly and opens a real java.net.Socket in checkActivate. It is not a simulated world network. The connect occurs before setSoTimeout, which is a read timeout rather than a connect limit.
impact: This leftover does not provide terminals, hacking, radio traffic or a saved local network for offline worlds. Its restricted tool status should not be confused with ordinary player gameplay.
repair: Keep legacy tooling explicitly separate; create an entirely simulated, game-clock network for content. Do not repurpose real sockets as fictional ship communications.
acceptance: Player terminal/radio interactions run offline, persist in saves, respect discovered nodes and access rights, and never require an external connection.

title: Existing tests do not establish an integrated sci-fi play loop
evidence: The S24 station and cutter fixtures both instantiate Asteroid, rename them, and verify position/count restoration. They do not exercise GenSpaceShip interiors, crew, power or software. Spaceangles was rerun and reproduced OF Test #5 failed: 360.0,0.0; Spaceinterception/2 are recorded baseline failures but were not rerun in this audit.
impact: Passing asset/save fixtures does not prove that a powered, crewed ship survives a complete campaign cycle. Existing math failures need repair rather than permanent acceptance for new sci-fi work.
repair: Add focused integration fixtures and a small playable technology museum after repairs; preserve baseline labels until each failure has an independently justified fix.
acceptance: A clean-start station-to-shuttle scenario covers editing, publishing, actual play, pause/turns, save/restore and a second world; all advertised sci-fi paths have relevant tests.

title: Portable electronics can drain while inactive and go negative
evidence: StdTriCorder.tick decrements its power cycle outside the activated/owned-by-MOB gate. StdElecItem.setPowerRemaining stores any long without clamping. An inactive still-ticking tricorder can therefore be decremented below zero. Tick-registration lifetime was not dynamically traced.
impact: A discarded or switched-off device can accumulate negative charge. Saved invalid values complicate recharging and balance.
repair: Specify idle versus active draw, gate drain accordingly, and centralize store invariants with deliberate migration of old values.
acceptance: Inactive and active portable devices behave as documented across 100 pulses, pause, time jumps and restore; stores remain within their allowed bounds.

title: Thruster wear and failure feedback do not match their apparent intent
evidence: StdShipThruster multiplies usesRemaining by 100 when forming a wear fraction, so ordinary positive wear values bypass its reduction. Its no-thrust/non-aft power path reports insufficient_fuel even when that condition does not establish fuel exhaustion.
impact: Damaged equipment does not degrade as expected and maintenance/flight software receives misleading failure reasons. Fuel exhaustion also has separate shutdown handling.
repair: Use a documented wear curve and structured reason codes; distinguish stopped, unsupported port, uninstalled, unpowered and out-of-fuel states.
acceptance: A 25%-condition engine follows its selected curve; a lateral maneuver with fuel does not report fuel exhaustion; diagnostics and scripts receive the actual reason.
